test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Indirect speech.

"Dear daughter," she said caressing her cheeks, "have you come to comfort me in my time of need?"

options.text: Caressing her daughter's cheeks, she asked affectionately if she did come to comfort her in her time of need.
Caressing her daughter's cheeks, she asked affectionately if she had come to comfort her in her time of need.
Caressing her daughter's cheeks, she said affectionately if she has come to comfort her in her time of need.
Caressing her daughter's cheeks, she said affectionately if she had been coming to comfort her in her time of need.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting from direct to indirect speech, we follow these rules:
 
• The reporting verb "said" changes to "asked" since it is a question.
 
• The pronoun "you" changes to "she" as per the subject.
 
• The verb "have come" (present perfect) changes to "had come" (past perfect) in indirect speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *Caressing her daughter's cheeks, she asked affectionately if she had come to comfort her in her time of need.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because "did come" is grammatically incorrect in indirect speech.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect because "said affectionately if" is incorrect; "asked" should be used instead.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because "had been coming" changes the tense unnecessarily and alters the meaning.
